evidence: Receiving DO2 observations: ~9.5 mg/L at 50.0 h dropping to ~1.0 mg/L at 50.2 h and ~0.89 mg/L at 52.0 h — below the 2.0 mg/L minimum
Delayed assay P=3.108 g/L at 48 h (available 52 h), on an upward trajectory similar to source batches, indicating ongoing production worth retaining
Source batches (source-1/2/3) never fell below ~7.4 mg/L, confirming the receiving DO2 collapse is an abnormal transfer-limitation event

Physics forward model: estimated transfer multiplier 0.40 after a change at ~50 h; strong_feed_reduction gives min DO 0.87 mg/L and 9.4 post-decision below-limit hours vs 13.2 h for increase_air/combined, with ~194 kg product mass retained in all cases
All sensitivity members infeasible for every bounded action, so no bounded option fully satisfies the 2.0 mg/L constraint; strong_feed_reduction minimizes the violation
args.rationale: DO2 collapsed from ~9.5 to ~1.0 mg/L at 50.2 h and remains ~0.9 mg/L at the 52 h decision point — an acute oxygen-transfer limitation (model estimates transfer multiplier dropped to ~0.4) violating the 2.0 mg/L minimum. Product (3.11 g/L at 48 h) is still rising, so a stop would forfeit counted production. Among the bounded interventions, strong_feed_reduction (feed to 0.6×, air to 1.15×) most aggressively cuts oxygen uptake demand while raising supply: the nominal forward model shows it yields the highest minimum DO2 (~0.87 mg/L), the fewest post-decision below-limit hours (9.4 vs 13.2 for increase_air/combined), and retains essentially full product mass (~194 kg). No bounded action fully restores the 2.0 mg/L minimum, so this is damage limitation: recommend strong_feed_reduction plus urgent engineering investigation of the aeration/transfer fault.
args.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and imperfect; it flags all sensitivity members as infeasible even for strong_feed_reduction, so the true receiving-process response (hidden parameters, actual OUR and kLa after 50 h) is uncertain — actual recovery could be better or worse than the nominal 0.87 mg/L minimum. The cause of the transfer drop (equipment fault vs. rheology change) is unobserved; if the fault worsens, even feed cutback may not restore DO2, whereas if transient, the batch may recover faster than predicted. Assay data are delayed 4 h, so current biomass/product state at 52 h is inferred, not measured.
